source.title: Stability Analysis of Sharpness-Aware Minimization
source.authors: Hoki Kim; Jinseong Park; Yu-Jin Choi; Jaewoo Lee

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some figure text is garbled, and several plotted values are not recoverable from the text.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports that larger batches make SAM harder to optimize and harm test accuracy in its CIFAR experiments, qualifying the large-batch generalization claim by optimizer and setup.
record.gate_note: The paper’s main focus is SAM’s convergence instability near saddle points. The CIFAR batch-size experiment directly reports train loss and test accuracy; most individual plotted values are available only as figures. Results cited from other studies were not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The fixed 300-epoch batch-size sweep measures held-out accuracy in a new optimizer setting, SAM. Figure 8 explicitly reports better performance with smaller batches, supporting V5 in this setting rather than qualifying it.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: theoretical and empirical analyses identify possible saddle-point trapping under SAM, and the CIFAR experiments show that smaller batches and higher momentum improve convergence and test accuracy. The authors acknowledge that SAM generally improves performance and that integrating these findings into more general settings remains open.
record.recipe_differences: Studies SAM’s convergence instability and training dynamics near saddle points; CIFAR batch-size experiments use SAM rather than the original large-batch SGD comparison.
record.method_sensitivity: For SAM, the reported outcome changes with batch size and momentum; the CIFAR batch-size experiments turn off batch normalization and data augmentation.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing momentum improves SAM's training convergence and test accuracy; its accuracy improvement exceeds 20 percentage points in Figure 9, versus approximately 5 for SGD.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAM's optimization and held-out performance can depend strongly on momentum.

fits_no_version.finding: Theoretical analyses and toy experiments show that SAM can become trapped near saddle points.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAM can impede saddle-point escape under particular dynamics and perturbation settings.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: The batch-size test-accuracy comparison is not numerically reported in the text; the B = 512 result is stated only as less than 60%, and other plotted values are not recoverable. Experiments are limited to ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 under the stated settings.
record.rows_left_out: Other batch-size values and their plotted train-loss and test-accuracy values are shown in Figure 8 but cannot be reliably recovered from the supplied text; retained the explicit B = 512 test-accuracy statements for both datasets.

untested.parts: Width sweeps beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under different tuning budgets.

Language models; longer training; learning-rate scaling and warmup; batch-size comparisons with adapted normalization or regularization. Momentum interventions do not establish closure of the batch-size penalty against a smaller-batch baseline.
Dropout interventions and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness ranking generalization gaps among similarly fitted networks, including comparisons with norm and margin measures.
Removing memorized examples versus removing random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Unavailable exact smaller-batch accuracies do not make the explicitly stated directional effect partial. The large-batch penalty accompanies worse training fit, so these results do not isolate a generalization-gap increase at matched training performance. Other batch-size curves are already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Memorization of random labels and generalization on natural labels.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive optimizers compared with SGD or momentum SGD.
Language models; comparisons to smaller batches with an adapted recipe; effects of longer training, learning-rate scaling, warmup, normalization or regularization changes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other generalization measures.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the effect on test accuracy.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Trained SAM with batch size B = 512 for 300 epochs; batch normalization and data augmentation were off.
rows.note: The text states that B = 512 produced train loss exceeding 1 and poor generalization; it does not give the exact test accuracy or a numerical smaller-batch reference.
rows.check: Use smaller batches B=8, 32, 128 as the qualitative comparison baseline. Figure 8 and Section 4.4 establish the batch-size penalty despite unavailable exact comparison values. The below-60% statement is reported jointly rather than separately by dataset. Add normalized radius rho=0.1 and momentum gamma=0.0 to the conditions.

relationships.condition: ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 with SAM, normalized rho=0.1, momentum gamma=0.0, 300 epochs, and batch normalization and augmentation disabled
relationships.reason: R1 and R2, interpreted with Figure 8's explicit smaller-batch comparison, show worse test performance as batch size increases; B=512 also leaves training loss above 1.
relationships.display_finding: The study reports worse test performance with larger batches and elevated training loss at batch 512, but these comparisons remain unverified.
